tool.name: BSDWorms
tool.summary: Worms: multi-scale edges of a potential-field grid. The grid is upward continued to a series of levels and the edges (maxima of the horizontal gradient) are found at each, using Frank Horowitz's bsdwormer code.
tool.usage:
The source depth of an edge is roughly half the continuation height of the level it appears at (Jacobsen 1987).

Writes <grid>_worms.csv (points with the level as z) and the padded grid to the output folder, and optionally <grid>_worms.shp: 3D polylines (PolylineZ) with the level as Z.

The grid needs a coordinate system with an EPSG code.

param.name: in_raster
param.dialogReference: Grid to process (a single-band raster; no-data cells are left as no-data in the result).
param.pythonReference: Grid to process (a single-band raster; no-data cells are left as no-data in the result).

param.name: out_dir
param.dialogReference: Folder for the worms CSV, the padded grid and the optional shapefile.
param.pythonReference: Folder for the worms CSV, the padded grid and the optional shapefile.

param.name: save_shp
param.dialogReference: Also write the worms as a 3D polyline shapefile (can be slow; best with the base level at 2000 m or more).
param.pythonReference: Also write the worms as a 3D polyline shapefile (can be slow; best with the base level at 2000 m or more).
